title: Request Stitching and Session Coalescing Design Spec
author: Priya Nair
summary: A design specification for combining related request fragments into coherent inference sessions ("request stitching") and opportunistically coalescing concurrent tenant sessions onto shared backend resources to reduce per-token cost and KV-cache churn while meeting latency SLOs and tenant isolation constraints.
body:
Overview

This spec defines Request Stitching and Session Coalescing: two coordinated features intended to reduce redundant KV cache warmups, increase effective GPU utilization, and lower per-token costs for multi-request conversational workloads. Request Stitching means merging logically related partial requests (e.g., multi-turn fragments, document-chunked prompts, or streaming deltas) into a single served session when semantics and safety rules allow. Session Coalescing means routing and packing concurrent short-lived or low-fidelity sessions from multiple tenants onto a smaller number of backend model sessions when policy permits.

This document covers goals, constraints, high-level design, API/contract changes, configuration examples, SLO and telemetry requirements, rollout plan, testing and backwards-compatibility considerations, and ownership.

Motivation

- Many customers send bursty conversational traffic composed of short partial updates. Each update causes KV cache overhead and repeated kernel scheduling.
- Cold KV cache population is a top driver of tail latency for LLM conversational workloads and increases per-token GPU time for short requests.
- Dedicated short sessions waste context window compute and reduce packing efficiency.

Goals

1. Reduce average per-token GPU time for conversational workloads by 10–30% for qualifying traffic classes.
2. Maintain per-route p95 latency within existing SLOs (default p95 < 250ms for interactive tiers) for requests eligible for stitching/coalescing.
3. Preserve tenant isolation and auditability; coalescing must never allow cross-tenant data leakage.

Non-goals

- This spec does not change fundamental billing semantics. Billing implications are surfaced as warnings and telemetry; commercial pricing changes are out of scope for the initial technical rollout.
- We will not implement cross-tenant prompt content sharing; session coalescing only shares runtime state when explicitly permitted by policy (see "Affinity & Privacy").

Key concepts and terminology

- Stitchable request: a request identified as semantically mergeable with previous open session fragments by the client or router heuristics (e.g., 'append', 'stream-delta', 'followup').
- Session affinity key: an opaque key used to bind an incoming request to an in-memory model session (can be tenant-level, route-level, or client-provided).
- Coalescing window: a short time window (e.g., 50–500ms) during which compatible short sessions may be co-located onto a single backend session.
body_2:
Design overview

1) Stitching Model
- API contract: new optional field in generation/chat payload: "stitch_instruction" (enum: none, append, replace, merge_safely) and "stitch_id" (string).
- Server behavior: when stitch_instruction != none and a matching open session (stitch_id) exists, router will route the fragment into the existing session's stream of tokens rather than creating a new KV context.
- Safety checks: compatibility validation includes model family compatibility, pinned model version, request temperature/fidelity thresholds, tokenization alignment check, and per-tenant policy. If validation fails, fallback to normal routing and emit a telemetry event.

2) Session Coalescing Model
- Coalescing is driven by a policy expression attached to tenant entitlements: "allow_coalesce: true|false" and an operational predicate: {max_context_fidelity, max_token_budget, allowed_model_variants}.
- The router maintains short-lived coalesce pools per region and model variant. Eligible sessions are placed into a pool for up to the configured coalescing window. When pool scheduling triggers, the runtime will instantiate as few backend sessions as feasible and map multiple logical sessions into the runtime with strict per-session boundaries enforced at the prompt/result layer.
- Coalescing will not share raw prompt text in-memory across tenants; instead, the runtime uses a multiplexing layer ensuring per-session token isolation in compute kernels and maintaining separate KV namespaces.

3) Affinity & Privacy
- Affinity levels: 
  - tenant_affinity: only same-tenant requests may be coalesced (default for regulated customers).
  - route_affinity: same tenant + same route (stronger isolation).
  - cross_tenant_shared: cross-tenant coalescing allowed only when tenants opt-in and have identical model fidelity constraints.
- Coalescing is disabled automatically for routes with PII classification, high-sensitivity labels, or when KMS-wrapped keys require dedicated HSM-backed sessions.

4) KV and Cache lifecycle changes
- Each logical session maintains a virtual KV namespace id. Backend runtime preserves separate KV keys per logical session to avoid contamination. To reduce duplication, runtime implements "sparse prefix reuse": when two sessions share an identical recent prefix, the kernel re-uses precomputed attention artifacts but still enforces namespace separation.

API changes and examples

- New optional fields for generation/chat API (HTTP/JSON):

  {
    "stitch_id": "string (optional - opaque)",
    "stitch_instruction": "none|append|merge_safely|replace",
    "coalesce_preference": "auto|tenant_affinity|route_affinity|deny",
    "session_ttl_ms": "integer (optional)"
  }

- Example: appending a chunked document: 

  POST /v1/generate
  {
    "model": "rwd-llama-70b-econ-v1",
    "stitch_id": "doc-12345-chunk-1",
    "stitch_instruction": "append",
    "input": "First chunk of a long document..."
  }

Operational configuration table

| Setting | Default | Purpose | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| coalesce_window_ms | 100 | How long router holds eligible sessions to attempt packing | eng-platform |
| max_coalesce_per_backend | 12 | Max logical sessions per backend runtime instance | eng-serving-runtime |
| stitch_validation_timeout_ms | 30 | Timeout in router for compatibility checks | eng-platform |
| tenant_opt_out_label | "no-coalesce" | Tenant label to disable automatic coalescing | customer-success |
SLOs and telemetry

- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for coalesced and non-coalesced paths must be tracked separately. Baseline SLO: coalesced p95 <= non-coalesced p95 + 40ms.
- Cost: track GPU-ms per-token and compare coalesced vs baseline per tenant segment.
- Correctness: monitor stitch-fallback-rate (number of stitch attempts that fell back to normal routing) and stitch-reorder-rate (cases where appending changed logical response ordering). Acceptable initial thresholds: stitch-fallback-rate < 5% and stitch-reorder-rate < 0.05%.
- Security: audit logs for any session coalesce actions, including affinity decision, participating tenant IDs, and decision reason.

Rollout plan

1) Canary (2 weeks): opt-in internal tenants + a small set of low-sensitivity beta customers. Metrics: latency, GPU-ms/token, fallback-rate. Blocker criteria: coalesced p95 worse than baseline p95 by > 60ms for > 10% of requests.
2) Beta (6 weeks): broader self-serve opt-in for customers with normal sensitivity. Provide UI toggle in Console and API flags. Add billing telemetry but no pricing changes.
3) Default-on for host/standard (3 months): flip default to on for non-restricted tenants; provide a 30-day notice and migration guidance.
4) Enterprise mode (parallel): for regulated tenants, provide dedicated per-tenant coalesce pools with tenant_affinity enforced.

Migration and compatibility notes

- Existing clients not sending stitch fields operate unchanged (stitch_instruction defaults to none).
- Customers that currently expect strict per-request billing may observe a small shift in cost-per-token telemetry due to reduced overheads; we will surface this in the Console under "Cost Insights -> Session Coalescing".

Testing matrix

- Unit tests: router decision logic for stitch compatibility, pool placement, TTL expiry.
- Integration: runtime isolation tests validating KV namespace separation under heavy coalesce packing (simulated multi-tenant traffic).
- Perf: synthetic conversational workloads with varying fragment sizes to validate GPU-ms/token improvements and tail latency.
- Security: adversarial mixing tests ensuring no prompt leakage across tenant boundaries.

Instrumentation and dashboards

- New dashboards: 
  - "Session Coalesce Overview" (global coalesce rate, average pool fill, avg coalesce window time)
  - "Tenant Coalesce Health" (per-tenant cost delta, fallback-rate, opt-out status)
  - "Stitch Errors" (reasons: model mismatch, pin mismatch, validation timeout)

Ownership and runbooks

- Owners: 
  - Product: Priya Nair (strategy + customer communication)
  - Eng Platform: Evan Brooks (router/policy)
  - Serving Runtime: Lina Gomez (runtime multiplexing, KV semantics)
- Runbook outlines: failure modes and mitigation. Examples: 
  - If coalesce backend saturates -> throttle new coalesce pools and revert to non-coalesced routing. Notify oncall and adjust coalesce_window_ms down by 50%.
  - If stitch_reorder_rate rises above threshold -> temporarily disable stitching for affected routes and create hotfix that forces strict session ordering.

Open questions (for review)

1. Billing model: should we expose a "coalesce credit" for customers who opt-out but want to pay for dedicated runtime? Recommend cross-team sync with Finance.
2. Deterministic replay: how do we guarantee exact response replay for stitched sessions when a fragment was merged and later trimmed? Proposal: store a lightweight fragment log per logical session for 48 hours.
3. Opt-in UX: should the Console provide per-route default and per-route overrides or a single tenant-level toggle?

Appendix: CLI/Debugging examples

- Inspect router decision for an incoming request:
  $ redwoodctl debug router --request-id=abcd-1234
  Decision: stitch_attempted=true, stitch_id=doc-12345-chunk-1, decision_reason=compatible, pool_id=coalesce-us-west-3-42

- Sample telemetry event (JSON shown for diagnostics):
  {
    "event": "stitch_attempt",
    "request_id": "abcd-1234",
    "stitch_id": "doc-12345-chunk-1",
    "decision": "fallback",
    "reason": "model_mismatch"
  }

Related work and references

- See runtime KV cache lifecycle document for sparse prefix reuse algorithm.
- Prior PRD: Predictive Batching & Cost Optimizer (2026-03-01) for performance baselining.

Summary and next steps

If approved, engineering teams will begin implementation in the router and runtime multiplexing layers per the rollout plan. Product will prepare documentation, migration notes, and Console toggles for customer opt-in. Finance and Sales will be engaged to review billing implications before defaulting this behavior on for any customers.
